headline: 14 minutes at the podium. An ambassador is out.
summary: Katie Zacharia took the White House podium for the first time Tuesday. The briefing ran 14 minutes, with a handful of questions at the end. Her news: Trump has asked Kimberly Guilfoyle, his ambassador to Greece, to resign. A donor says Guilfoyle asked him to pay a $100,000 credit card bill in exchange for access. She calls that false.

cover_question.q: What does a press secretary do?

cover_answer: Speaks for the president. Takes questions, or doesn't.
table_question: Would you drop a friend over a rule they say they didn't break?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: The president has a new helper whose job is to tell reporters what he is doing. Her name is Katie Zacharia. On her first day she stood at a podium for 14 minutes, shorter than recess. Her big news was that a lady who worked for the president in Greece has to stop, because someone says she asked for money she should not have. The grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: A new helper and a short talk. The money part stays one sentence.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, so the script gives them a person, a podium and 14 minutes measured against recess. Greece is one sentence: a bribe is a chain they cannot follow yet. Expect "is she a bad lady?" Someone says she broke a rule, she says she didn't, and the grown-ups are checking.

8-12.script: A newspaper says Guilfoyle, the ambassador to Greece, asked a donor to pay her $100,000 credit card bill and offered meetings with officials back. The donor said no. Tuesday Trump asked her to resign. A hall monitor can't sell hall passes, even if nobody buys.
8-12.why: Report, ask, resign: a chain in order, then the hall-pass rule.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out whether adults apply rules consistently, so the script runs the chain in order: a report, a refusal, a resignation. The hall pass is the rule underneath, that you cannot sell what the job gives you. Expect "but she didn't get the money." Asking is the problem, if she asked. She says she didn't.

13-17.script: Trump has stood by plenty of officials accused of using their office for gain. Why not this one? He said "I didn't like what I was reading." Second: the new press secretary says her job is promoting the president's message. Her first briefing took a handful of questions in 14 minutes. Who is a briefing for?
13-17.why: Two questions to argue: why this ally, and who the podium serves.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: Trump parted with a longtime ally over a bribery claim, and he has kept others through worse. Then the second question, who a briefing is for, which 14 minutes and a handful of questions let them judge. Expect "did she do it?" Nobody knows yet. An inspector general is looking.

5-7.a: The lady in Greece might. She says she did nothing wrong. The new helper did fine; the president said so.

8-12.q: What does a press secretary do?
8-12.a: Speaks for the president and takes reporters' questions.

8-12.q: Why did the ambassador have to quit?
8-12.a: A donor says she offered access for $100,000. She says it's false.

13-17.q: Is asking a donor to pay your bill a crime?
13-17.a: The articles don't say. An inspector general is reviewing it.

13-17.q: Does the press secretary have to answer questions?
13-17.a: No rule says so. She sent Guilfoyle questions to the president.

caption:
Speaks for the president. Takes questions, or doesn't.

Katie Zacharia took the White House podium for the first time Tuesday. The briefing ran 14 minutes, with a handful of questions at the end. Her news: Trump has asked Kimberly Guilfoyle, his ambassador to Greece, to resign. A donor says Guilfoyle asked him to pay a $100,000 credit card bill in exchange for access. She calls that false.

Source: PBS NewsHour
